name: Realistic Timeline for a Full Kitchen Overhaul in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: How long does a full kitchen overhaul typically take in Los Angeles County once permits are filed, and what delays are common with local inspections?
mainEntity.text: How long does a full kitchen overhaul typically take in Los Angeles County once permits are filed, and what delays are common with local inspections?

acceptedAnswer.text: Timeline for a full kitchen overhaul in Los Angeles County is heavily influenced by permitting, inspection schedules, and material readiness. After design and selections are finalized, many contractors estimate 8–14 weeks of active construction for a complete overhaul, including demolition, rough plumbing and electrical, inspections, drywall, cabinets, countertops, and finishes. However, the clock often starts earlier with plan check; depending on your city, reviews and re‑submittals can add 2–6 weeks before major work begins. During construction, expect a sequence of inspections: usually rough plumbing, electrical, and framing before insulation and drywall, then final inspections at the end. In busy periods, getting an inspection slot can push the schedule by several days. Delays also arise from back‑ordered cabinets, custom countertops, or specialty appliances that must be on site for accurate measurements and proper rough‑in locations. If inspectors flag items for correction—such as missing nail plates, outlet spacing, or venting—your contractor must fix them and call for re‑inspection, which can add a week or more. To manage expectations, ask your contractor for a written schedule with milestones and a list of items you must select or purchase early so inspections and trades are not waiting on materials.
acceptedAnswer.description: A full kitchen overhaul in Los Angeles County typically takes 8–14 weeks after permits are filed, depending on design complexity and structural work. Homeowners should anticipate potential delays from plan check comments, inspection availability, back‑ordered materials, and required corrections on electrical, plumbing, or framing before drywall can be closed.
